2.Hydroelectricenergy
The world's second most popular source of electricity
after coal is hydroelectric power. It generates
electricity from the rapid flow of water.Usuallya
largehydropowersystemusesadamtostoreriver
water in reservoir. Water released from the reservoir
flows through a turbine, spinning it, which in turn
activates a generator to produce electricity. Many
developing countries depend on hydroelectric
power for majority of their electricity. Pakistan has
been ranked third in the world for newly installed
hydropower capacityin2018 alongwithChina and
Brazilrespectively
Hydroelectric energy
3.Windenergy

The process by which the wind is used to generate
electricity is called wind energy. It is the most
developed renewable energy resource. Large wind
mills calledwind turbinesproduceelectricityfromthe
wind. In order to create electricity supplies to people,
energy companies build large wind farms of wind
turbines in windy places. Jiuquan Wind Power Base,
China, is the world's biggest wind farm, with a planned
installed capacity of 20GW.It is alsoknown as Gansu
Wind Farm.Wind energymakes up more than 6 percent
of total electricity production in Pakistan.The coastal
line of Sindh is most suitable for wind farms. In
Pakistan, Jhimpir is part of "Gharo-Jhimpir" in Sindh
stretching on 180 km of costal land.
